claims.mitigation_description: Every consequential agent decision emits a signed Intent Decision Record (IDR) into an append-only chain: a per-record signature over the entry hash (HMAC-SHA256 in the hermetic standard-library core; Ed25519, ML-DSA-65 or both as asymmetric backends), predecessor linkage inside the signed body, and an RFC-6962 Merkle root over the records in chain order. Any byte alteration is detectable by recomputation. The engine's source code is public; the records themselves are not, and the verification is arithmetic, not attestation.

The chain's Merkle root is committed to Bitcoin via OpenTimestamps, so even the record custodian cannot rewrite history undetectably. The production decision-chain root 0bba0792bf9f71caa815d0c42daf27f45baf07ef9749523be666f103a7f1bcb4 (501 records) is attested in Bitcoin blocks 956991 and 956992. The anchor manifest, the upgraded OpenTimestamps proof and the 501 RFC-6962 leaf hashes are published, so any party can re-derive the root from the leaf hashes and check the proof against a public block explorer with no trust in the authors.

Every outward claim carries a receipt binding it to a verbatim quotation at recorded byte offsets in a content-addressed source. Citation verification is deterministic and model-free: a quotation that is not verbatim in its source (exact, then whitespace- and typography-flexible matching) records as not_found, and in strict mode any not_found raises and stops the deliverable. Two independent verifiers disagreeing on a citation's status or offsets for the same inputs would falsify this claim.

Verification and replay are pure, deterministic, standard-library re-derivations executable by any third party offline: re-hash, re-verify signatures, re-walk the Merkle path, re-derive the replay digest (byte-identical across machines and providers; no language model on the path). The claimant's own report is never the criterion (exogenous-anchor law). Two independent replays of an unchanged record set that disagree would falsify this claim.
